summary: inclusionAI's Ming-3.0-tts: speaks Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, German, French and Spanish at 44.1 kHz in the speaker's own voice, cloned from the video, in one of its built-in voices, or in a voice made from a description, with emotion and speed controls. Heavy: a 2.99 GB model downloaded on first use and about 5 GB of memory; on a CPU each second of speech takes about four seconds to make.
author: Subtitld

voices.display_name: Speaker's own voice (cloned from the video)
Ling Xiaorou (Chinese woman, clear and patient)
Ling Kai (Chinese man, warm late-night radio)

fields.label: Inference device
fields.help: This build runs on the CPU. The GPU of an Apple Silicon Mac may work but has not been tried. It does not use NVIDIA GPUs.

fields.label: CPU threads
fields.help: 0 picks the performance cores on a CPU that also has efficiency cores, else one thread per core. Fewer leaves the computer more responsive while dubbing.

fields.label: Emotion
fields.help: For the speaker's own voice and the described voices: speak every line with this emotion. It keeps only the speaker's timbre, not their way of speaking, and overrides the speed, pitch and volume below. Built-in voices ignore it.

fields.label: Speed
fields.help: For the speaker's own voice and the described voices, when no emotion is set. Like the emotion, it keeps only the speaker's timbre.

fields.label: Voice description
fields.help: For the voice 'Voice you describe': who speaks and how, in a few words, for example 'An elderly woman, soft and warm voice, slow pace'. English or Chinese works for every language.

fields.label: Fallback reference clip
fields.help: Used by the speaker's own voice when Subtitld has no clip of the speaker to send: 3 to 10 seconds of one person speaking, WAV preferred.

fields.label: Fallback reference transcript
fields.help: The exact words spoken in the fallback clip. With them the clone is closer to the speaker.

fields.label: Clone the timbre only
fields.help: Subtitld normally sends, with the speaker's clip, the subtitle text spoken in it, and Ming-3.0-tts then continues from the clip, which comes closest to the speaker. With this on, only the timbre is cloned. Try it if a dub into another language keeps the speaker's accent, or when the subtitles paraphrase the speech.
